    self.sfr[SFR_PSW] = psw | _PARITY[value]
On real silicon ADD/ADDC/SUBB always *update* CY, AC and OV (set or clear). Here they are sticky-on. The `& 0xC0` mask additionally wipes PSW bits 3..5 (RS0/RS1/F0), i.e. any ADD switches the register bank back to bank 0 — that will break real firmware that uses banks 1..3.

MEASURED (unmodified core):
    MOV A,#08h / ADD A,#08h      ; AC=1
    MOV A,#10h / ADD A,#01h      ; no nibble carry -> AC must clear
    DA  A                        ; correct result: 10h
    -> actual: 17h   (DA saw the stale AC and added 6)
    MOV A,#0FFh / ADD A,#02h     ; CY=1
    MOV A,#01h  / ADD A,#01h     ; CY must clear
    -> actual CY still 1
    BCD idiom  MOV A,#50h / ADD A,#00h / DA A   (with a stale AC)
    -> actual: 56h, correct: 50h

FIX (build the flag bits from scratch, preserve RS0/RS1/F0 = 0x38):
    def _add(self, operand: int, carry_in: int) -> None:
        a = self.sfr[SFR_ACC]
        carry = 1 if carry_in else 0
        result = a + operand + carry
        psw = self.sfr[SFR_PSW] & 0x38          # keep RS0, RS1, F0 only
        if ((a & 0x0F) + (operand & 0x0F) + carry) > 0x0F:
            psw |= 0x40                          # AC
        if result > 0xFF:
            psw |= 0x80                          # CY
        value = result & 0xFF
        if (a ^ value) & (operand ^ value) & 0x80:
            psw |= 0x04                          # OV
        self.sfr[SFR_ACC] = value
        self.sfr[SFR_PSW] = psw | _PARITY[value]

    def _sub(self, operand: int, carry_in: int) -> None:
        a = self.sfr[SFR_ACC]
        borrow = 1 if carry_in else 0
        result = a - operand - borrow
        psw = self.sfr[SFR_PSW] & 0x38
        if ((a & 0x0F) - (operand & 0x0F) - borrow) < 0:
            psw |= 0x40
        if result < 0:
            psw |= 0x80
        value = result & 0xFF
        if (a ^ operand) & (a ^ value) & 0x80:
            psw |= 0x04
        self.sfr[SFR_ACC] = value
        self.sfr[SFR_PSW] = psw | _PARITY[value]

`_da()` itself is fine once AC/CY are trustworthy. Note DA A is the standard 8051 BCD idiom, so this bug affects any real firmware doing decimal money arithmetic, not just my demo.

212:         self.sfr[SFR_P1] = 0xFF
213:         self.sfr[SFR_P2] = 0xFF
214:         self.sfr[SFR_P3] = 0xFF

217:         self.pc = 0
218:         self.cycles = 0
219:         self.op_count = 0
220:         self.halted = False
221:         self.error = None
222:         self.missing_pc = None
223:         self.in_isr = 0
224:         self.irq_level = 0
225:         self.idle = False
226:         self.watchdog = 0
227:         self.wd_enabled = False

232:     # ----------------------------------------------------------------- helpers
233:     @property
234:     def acc(self) -> int:
235:         return self.sfr[SFR_ACC]
236: 
237:     @acc.setter
238:     def acc(self, value: int) -> None:
239:         self.sfr[SFR_ACC] = value & 0xFF

241:     @property
242:     def psw(self) -> int:
243:         return self.sfr[SFR_PSW]
244:

248: 
249:     def set_p(self) -> None:
250:         p = _PARITY[self.sfr[SFR_ACC]]
251:         self.sfr[SFR_PSW] = (self.sfr[SFR_PSW] & 0xFE) | p

253:     @property
254:     def sp(self) -> int:
255:         return self.sfr[SFR_SP]
256: 
257:     @sp.setter
258:     def sp(self, value: int) -> None:
259:         self.sfr[SFR_SP] = value & 0xFF
260: 
261:     @property
262:     def dptr(self) -> int:
263:         return self.sfr[SFR_DPH] << 8 | self.sfr[SFR_DPL]
264: 
265:     @dptr.setter
266:     def dptr(self, value: int) -> None:
267:         self.sfr[SFR_DPH] = (value >> 8) & 0xFF

270:     # register bank helpers (indirect through PSW.RS0/RS1)
271:     def _r(self, n: int) -> int:
272:         return self.ram[((self.sfr[SFR_PSW] >> 3) & 3) * 8 + n]
273: 
274:     def _set_r(self, n: int, v: int) -> None:
275:         self.ram[((self.sfr[SFR_PSW] >> 3) & 3) * 8 + n] = v & 0xFF
276: 
277:     def _ri(self, n: int) -> int:
278:         """Address held in R0/R1 of the active bank."""
279:         return self.ram[((self.sfr[SFR_PSW] >> 3) & 3) * 8 + n]

281:     # ------------------------------------------------------------------- stack
282:     def push(self, value: int) -> None:
283:         sp = (self.sfr[SFR_SP] + 1) & 0xFF

285:         self.ram[sp] = value & 0xFF
286:         if sp <= 7:

289:     def pop(self) -> int:
290:         sp = self.sfr[SFR_SP]
291:         value = self.ram[sp]
292:         self.sfr[SFR_SP] = (sp - 1) & 0xFF

295:     def push_pc(self) -> None:
296:         """Push the return address the way silicon does: low byte, then high.
297: 
298:         ``RET``/``RETI`` pop the high byte first (see :meth:`pop_pc`), so pushing
299:         high first would byte-swap every return address and corrupt control flow
300:         for every ``LCALL``/``ACALL`` and every interrupt.
301:         """
302:         pc = self.pc
303:         self.push(pc & 0xFF)
304:         self.push(pc >> 8)
305:         if self.in_isr < 8:
306:             self.in_isr += 1

308:     def pop_pc(self) -> None:
309:         high = self.pop()
310:         low = self.pop()
311:         self.pc = (high << 8) | low
312:         if self.in_isr:
313:             self.in_isr -= 1
314: 
315:     # ------------------------------------------------------------- direct/bit
316:     def _dir_read(self, addr: int) -> int:
317:         if addr < 0x80:
318:             return self.ram[addr]
319:         return self.sfr[addr]
320: 
321:     def _dir_write(self, addr: int, value: int) -> None:
322:         value &= 0xFF
323:         if addr < 0x80:
324:             self.ram[addr] = value
325:             return
326:         if addr == SFR_ACC:
327:             self.sfr[SFR_ACC] = value
328:             self.set_p()
329:             return
330:         if addr == SFR_PSW:
331:             self.sfr[SFR_PSW] = value
332:             return
333:         if SFR_P0 <= addr <= SFR_P3 and (addr & 0x0F) == 0:
334:             # ports need pin/latch interaction
335:             port = (addr - SFR_P0) >> 4
336:             self._port_latch[port] = value
337:             self.sfr[addr] = value
338:             self.bus.port_write(port, value)
339:             return
340:         self.sfr[addr] = value
341:         if addr == SFR_SBUF:
342:             self.bus.serial_write(value)
343:             self.sfr[SFR_SCON] |= SCON_TI
344:         self._sfr_side_effect(addr, value)
345: 
346:     def _port_read(self, port: int) -> int:
347:         """Read a port: latch AND external pin levels (quasi-bidirectional)."""
348:         return self._port_latch[port] & self.bus.port_read(port)
349: 
350:     def _sfr_side_effect(self, addr: int, value: int) -> None:
351:         if addr == SFR_WDTRST:
352:             self.watchdog = 0
353:         elif addr == SFR_WDTPRG:
354:             self.wd_enabled = True
355:         elif addr == SFR_TCON:
356:             self.timers_on = (value & 0x50) != 0
357:         elif addr == SFR_SCON:
358:             self._serial_rx = bool(value & SCON_REN) and self.bus.serial_available()
359: 
360:     # -------------------------------------------------------------------- time
361:     def _advance(self, cycles: int) -> None:
362:         """Run timers/serial/peripherals for ``cycles`` machine cycles."""
363:         self.cycles += cycles
364:         self.op_count += 1
365:         if self.timers_on or self.wd_enabled or self._serial_rx:
366:             self._do_peripherals(cycles)
367:         elif self._pending_tick:
368:             self._pending_tick += cycles
369:             if self._pending_tick >= 32:
370:                 self.bus.tick(self._pending_tick)
371:                 self._pending_tick = 0
372:         else:
373:             self._pending_tick = cycles
374: 
375:     @staticmethod
376:     def _tick_timer(mode: int, th: int, tl: int, cycles: int):
377:         """Advance one 8051 timer by ``cycles`` machine cycles.
378: 
379:         Returns ``(th, tl, overflowed)``.  Each of the four modes is handled by
380:         its own arithmetic; doing it in one 16-bit addition is wrong, because a
381:         multi-cycle batch would be applied to the reloaded value (mode 2 reloads
382:         the low byte from the high byte on every overflow, so the batch has to
383:         be consumed overflow by overflow).
384: 
385:         * mode 0 - 13-bit timer (``TH`` holds 5 bits)
386:         * mode 1 - 16-bit timer
387:         * mode 2 - 8-bit auto-reload: ``TL`` counts, reloads from ``TH``
388:         * mode 3 - split: ``TL`` is an independent 8-bit timer, ``TH`` is
389:           stopped (it belongs to the other timer)
390:         """
391:         if mode == 0:
392:             value = ((th & 0x1F) << 8 | tl) + cycles
393:             overflowed = value > 0x1FFF
394:             if overflowed:
395:                 value &= 0x1FFF
396:             return (value >> 8) & 0x1F, value & 0xFF, overflowed
397:         if mode == 1:
398:             value = (th << 8 | tl) + cycles
399:             overflowed = value > 0xFFFF
400:             if overflowed:
401:                 value &= 0xFFFF
402:             return (value >> 8) & 0xFF, value & 0xFF, overflowed
403:         if mode == 2:
404:             # TL counts up from its current value to 0xFF, overflows, reloads
405:             # from TH, then counts again.  One overflow takes ``256 - reload``
406:             # cycles, so the batch must be consumed overflow by overflow instead
407:             # of being added to the reloaded value in one go (doing the latter
408:             # corrupts TH, which is the reload register and must never change).
409:             reload = th & 0xFF
410:             period = 256 - reload
411:             remaining = tl + cycles
412:             overflowed = remaining > 0xFF
413:             if overflowed:
414:                 remaining -= 0x100
415:                 while remaining >= period:
416:                     remaining -= period
417:                 value = reload + remaining
418:             else:
419:                 value = remaining
420:             return reload, value & 0xFF, overflowed
421:         # mode 3: only the low half counts, the high half is stopped
422:         value = tl + cycles
423:         overflowed = value > 0xFF
424:         return th & 0xFF, value & 0xFF, overflowed
425: 
426:     def _do_peripherals(self, cycles: int) -> None:
427:         bus = self.bus
428:         if self._pending_tick:
429:             bus.tick(self._pending_tick + cycles)
430:             self._pending_tick = 0
431:         else:
432:             bus.tick(cycles)
433:         sfr = self.sfr
434:         tmod = sfr[SFR_TMOD]
435:         tcon = sfr[SFR_TCON]
436:         if tcon & TCON_TR0:
437:             th, tl, overflowed = self._tick_timer(
438:                 tmod & 0x03, sfr[SFR_TH0], sfr[SFR_TL0], cycles)
439:             sfr[SFR_TH0] = th
440:             sfr[SFR_TL0] = tl
441:             if overflowed:
442:                 tcon |= TCON_TF0
443:         if tcon & TCON_TR1:
444:             th, tl, overflowed = self._tick_timer(
445:                 (tmod >> 4) & 0x03, sfr[SFR_TH1], sfr[SFR_TL1], cycles)
446:             sfr[SFR_TH1] = th
447:             sfr[SFR_TL1] = tl
448:             if overflowed:
449:                 tcon |= TCON_TF1
450:         sfr[SFR_TCON] = tcon
451:         self.timers_on = (tcon & 0x50) != 0
452:         # serial receive
453:         if self._serial_rx:
454:             chunk = bus.serial_read()
455:             if chunk is not None:
456:                 sfr[SFR_SBUF] = chunk & 0xFF
457:                 sfr[SFR_SCON] |= SCON_RI
458:         # watchdog: 8051 WDT overflows ~ 2**17 machine cycles on AT89C55
459:         if self.wd_enabled:
460:             self.watchdog += cycles
461:             if self.watchdog > 0x20000:
462:                 self.watchdog = 0
463: 
464:     # ------------------------------------------------------------ interrupts
465:     def _poll_interrupts(self) -> None:
466:         ie = self.sfr[SFR_IE]
467:         if not (ie & 0x80):            # EA
468:             return
469:         pending = 0
470:         tcon = self.sfr[SFR_TCON]
471:         if tcon & TCON_IE0:
472:             pending |= IRQ_INT0
473:         if tcon & TCON_TF0:
474:             pending |= IRQ_T0
475:         if tcon & TCON_IE1:
476:             pending |= IRQ_INT1
477:         if tcon & TCON_TF1:
478:             pending |= IRQ_T1
479:         if self.sfr[SFR_SCON] & SCON_RI:
480:             pending |= IRQ_RX
481:         if self.sfr[SFR_SCON] & SCON_TI:
482:             pending |= IRQ_TX
483:         pending |= self.bus.irq_requested()
484:         pending &= 0xFF
485:         if not pending:
486:             return
487:         ip = self.sfr[SFR_IP]
488:         chosen = -1
489:         chosen_pri = -1
490:         for bit, irq in zip(range(6), _VEC_IRQ):
491:             if not (pending & irq):
492:                 continue
493:             if not (ie & irq):
494:                 continue
495:             if (ip & irq) and self.irq_level and irq != self.irq_level:
496:                 continue
497:             pri = 1 if (ip & irq) else 0
498:             if pri > chosen_pri:
499:                 chosen_pri = pri
500:                 chosen = bit
501:         if chosen < 0:
502:             return
503:         irq = _VEC_IRQ[chosen]
504:         if irq == IRQ_T0:
505:             self.sfr[SFR_TCON] &= ~TCON_TF0 & 0xFF
506:         elif irq == IRQ_T1:
507:             self.sfr[SFR_TCON] &= ~TCON_TF1 & 0xFF
508:         elif irq == IRQ_INT0:
509:             self.sfr[SFR_TCON] &= ~TCON_IE0 & 0xFF
510:         elif irq == IRQ_INT1:
511:             self.sfr[SFR_TCON] &= ~TCON_IE1 & 0xFF
512:         elif irq == IRQ_RX:
513:             self.sfr[SFR_SCON] &= ~SCON_RI & 0xFF
514:         elif irq == IRQ_TX:
515:             self.sfr[SFR_SCON] &= ~SCON_TI & 0xFF
516:         self.irq_level = irq if (ip & irq) else 0
517:         self._advance(2)
518:         self.push_pc()
519:         self.pc = _VEC[chosen]
520: 
521:     # ------------------------------------------------------------------- step
522:     def step(self) -> int:
523:         """Execute one instruction.  Returns the machine cycles consumed."""
524:         if self.halted:
525:             return 1
526:         if not self.rom.is_mapped(self.pc):
527:             # Fetching from an address that no code image covers.  On real
528:             # silicon this reads 0xFF (erased EPROM) and the CPU wanders; for
529:             # emulation that is useless, so we stop and report it.
530:             self.missing_pc = self.pc
531:             self.halted = True
532:             self.error = (f"fetch from unmapped code address 0x{self.pc:04X} "
533:                           f"- this part of the firmware image is missing")
534:             return 1
535:         if self.idle:
536:             self._advance(1)
537:             return 1
538:         self._poll_interrupts()
539:         cycles = self._execute()
540:         self._advance(cycles)
541:         return cycles
542: 
543:     def run_steps(self, max_steps: int) -> int:
544:         """Execute at most ``max_steps`` instructions; stop on halt/error."""
545:         executed = 0
546:         while executed < max_steps and not self.halted:
547:             if not self.rom.is_mapped(self.pc):
548:                 self.missing_pc = self.pc
549:                 self.halted = True
550:                 self.error = (f"fetch from unmapped code address 0x{self.pc:04X} "
551:                               f"- this part of the firmware image is missing")
552:                 break
553:             if self.idle:
554:                 self._advance(1)
555:             else:
556:                 self._poll_interrupts()
557:                 self._advance(self._execute())
558:             executed += 1
559:         return executed
560: 
561:     def run(self, cycles: int) -> int:
562:         """Run for at most ``cycles`` machine cycles (or forever if <= 0)."""
563:         executed = 0
564:         target = self.cycles + cycles if cycles > 0 else -1
565:         execute = self._execute
566:         advance = self._advance
567:         mapped = self.rom.is_mapped
568:         while True:
569:             if self.halted:
570:                 break
571:             if self.idle:
572:                 advance(1)
573:             else:
574:                 self._poll_interrupts()
575:                 advance(execute())
576:             executed += 1
577:             if target >= 0 and self.cycles >= target:
578:                 break
579:             if executed >= 400_000_000:
580:                 break
581:             if not mapped(self.pc):
582:                 self.missing_pc = self.pc
583:                 self.halted = True
584:                 self.error = (f"fetch from unmapped code address 0x{self.pc:04X} "
585:                               f"- this part of the firmware image is missing")
586:                 break
587:         return executed
588: 
589:     # --------------------------------------------------------------- execution
590:     def _execute(self) -> int:
591:         rom = self.rom
592:         pc = self.pc
593:         self.last_op = rom.byte(pc)
594:         trace = self.trace
595:         if trace is not None:
596:             if len(trace) < self.trace_limit:
597:                 trace.append((pc, self.last_op, self.acc, self.psw,
598:                               self.sfr[SFR_SP], self.cycles))
599:             else:
600:                 self.trace = None
601:         p = pc + 1
602:         op = self.last_op
603:         romb = rom.byte
604:         sfr = self.sfr
605:         ram = self.ram
606:         bus = self.bus
607:         # ---- decode/execute -------------------------------------------------
608:         if op == 0x00:                                              # NOP
609:             self.pc = p
610:             return 1
611:         # ================================ MOV A, #imm / direct / @Ri / Rn / R
612:         if op == 0x74:                                              # MOV A,#imm
613:             self.pc = p + 1
614:             self.acc = romb(p)
615:             return 1
616:         if op == 0xE5:                                              # MOV A,direct
617:             self.pc = p + 1
618:             addr = romb(p)
619:             if addr == SFR_ACC:
620:                 pass
621:             elif addr < 0x80:
622:                 self.acc = ram[addr]
623:             elif SFR_P0 <= addr <= SFR_P3 and (addr & 0x0F) == 0:
624:                 self.acc = self._port_read((addr - SFR_P0) >> 4)
625:             elif addr == SFR_SBUF:
626:                 self.acc = self.sfr[addr]
627:             else:
628:                 self.acc = self.sfr[addr]
629:             self.set_p()
630:             return 1
631:         if op == 0xF5:                                              # MOV direct,A
632:             self.pc = p + 1
633:             self._dir_write(romb(p), self.sfr[SFR_ACC])
634:             return 1
635:         if op == 0xE4:                                              # CLR A
636:             self.pc = p
637:             self.acc = 0
638:             return 1
639:         if op == 0xF4:                                              # CPL A
640:             self.pc = p
641:             self.acc = self.sfr[SFR_ACC] ^ 0xFF
642:             return 1
643:         if op in (0xE6, 0xE7):                                      # MOV A,@Ri
644:             self.pc = p
645:             self.acc = ram[self._ri(op & 1)]
646:             self.set_p()
647:             return 1
648:         if op in (0xF6, 0xF7):                                      # MOV @Ri,A
649:             self.pc = p
650:             ram[self._ri(op & 1)] = self.sfr[SFR_ACC]
651:             return 1
652:         if op in (0x76, 0x77):                                      # MOV @Ri,#imm
653:             self.pc = p + 1
654:             ram[self._ri(op & 1)] = romb(p)
655:             return 1
656:         if 0xE8 <= op <= 0xEF:                                      # MOV A,Rn
657:             self.pc = p
658:             self.acc = self._r(op & 7)
659:             self.set_p()
660:             return 1
661:         if 0xF8 <= op <= 0xFF:                                      # MOV Rn,A
662:             self.pc = p
663:             self._set_r(op & 7, self.sfr[SFR_ACC])
664:             return 1
665:         if 0x78 <= op <= 0x7F:                                      # MOV Rn,#imm
666:             self.pc = p + 1
667:             self._set_r(op & 7, romb(p))
668:             return 1
669:         if 0xA8 <= op <= 0xAF:                                      # MOV Rn,direct
670:             self.pc = p + 1
671:             self._set_r(op & 7, self._dir_read(romb(p)))
672:             return 1
673:         if 0x88 <= op <= 0x8F:                                      # MOV direct,Rn
674:             self.pc = p + 1
675:             self._dir_write(romb(p), self._r(op & 7))
676:             return 1
677:         if op == 0x85:                                             # MOV direct,direct
678:             self.pc = p + 2
679:             src = romb(p)
680:             dst = romb(p + 1)
681:             self._dir_write(dst, self._dir_read(src))
682:             return 2
683:         if op == 0x75:                                             # MOV direct,#imm
684:             self.pc = p + 2
685:             self._dir_write(romb(p), romb(p + 1))
686:             return 2
687:         if op in (0x86, 0x87):                                     # MOV direct,@Ri
688:             self.pc = p + 1
689:             self._dir_write(romb(p), ram[self._ri(op & 1)])
690:             return 2
691:         if op in (0xA6, 0xA7):                                     # MOV @Ri,direct
692:             self.pc = p + 1
693:             ram[self._ri(op & 1)] = self._dir_read(romb(p))
694:             return 2
695:         if op == 0x90:                                             # MOV DPTR,#imm16
696:             self.pc = p + 2
697:             self.sfr[SFR_DPH] = romb(p)
698:             self.sfr[SFR_DPL] = romb(p + 1)
699:             return 2
700:         # ============================== MOVC / MOVX
701:         if op == 0x93:                                             # MOVC A,@A+DPTR
702:             self.pc = p
703:             self.acc = romb((self.sfr[SFR_ACC] + self.dptr) & 0xFFFF)
704:             return 2
705:         if op == 0x83:                                             # MOVC A,@A+PC
706:             self.pc = p
707:             self.acc = romb((self.sfr[SFR_ACC] + p) & 0xFFFF)
708:             return 2
709:         if op in (0xE2, 0xE3):                                     # MOVX A,@Ri
710:             self.pc = p
711:             addr = self._ri(op & 1)
712:             if self.sfr[SFR_P2]:
713:                 addr |= self.sfr[SFR_P2] << 8
714:             self.acc = bus.ext_read(addr) & 0xFF
715:             self.set_p()
716:             return 2
717:         if op in (0xF2, 0xF3):                                     # MOVX @Ri,A
718:             self.pc = p
719:             addr = self._ri(op & 1)
720:             self._ext_write_banked(addr, self.sfr[SFR_ACC])
721:             return 2
722:         if op == 0xE0:                                             # MOVX A,@DPTR
723:             self.pc = p
724:             self.acc = bus.ext_read(self.dptr) & 0xFF
725:             self.set_p()
726:             return 2
727:         if op == 0xF0:                                             # MOVX @DPTR,A
728:             self.pc = p
729:             bus.ext_write(self.dptr, self.sfr[SFR_ACC])
730:             return 2
731:         if op == 0xA3:                                             # INC DPTR
732:             self.pc = p
733:             self.dptr = (self.dptr + 1) & 0xFFFF
734:             return 2
735:         # =============================================================== ADD
736:         if op == 0x24:                                             # ADD A,#imm
737:             self.pc = p + 1
738:             self._add(romb(p), 0)
739:             return 1
740:         if op == 0x25:                                             # ADD A,direct
741:             self.pc = p + 1
742:             self._add(self._dir_read(romb(p)), 0)
743:             return 1
744:         if op in (0x26, 0x27):                                     # ADD A,@Ri
745:             self.pc = p
746:             self._add(ram[self._ri(op & 1)], 0)
747:             return 1
748:         if 0x28 <= op <= 0x2F:                                     # ADD A,Rn
749:             self.pc = p
750:             self._add(self._r(op & 7), 0)
751:             return 1
752:         if op == 0x34:                                             # ADDC A,#imm
753:             self.pc = p + 1
754:             self._add(romb(p), sfr[SFR_PSW] & 0x80)
755:             return 1
756:         if op == 0x35:                                             # ADDC A,direct
757:             self.pc = p + 1
758:             self._add(self._dir_read(romb(p)), sfr[SFR_PSW] & 0x80)
759:             return 1
760:         if op in (0x36, 0x37):
761:             self.pc = p
762:             self._add(ram[self._ri(op & 1)], sfr[SFR_PSW] & 0x80)
763:             return 1
764:         if 0x38 <= op <= 0x3F:
765:             self.pc = p
766:             self._add(self._r(op & 7), sfr[SFR_PSW] & 0x80)
767:             return 1
768:         # =============================================================== SUBB
769:         if op == 0x94:
770:             self.pc = p + 1
771:             self._sub(romb(p), sfr[SFR_PSW] & 0x80)
772:             return 1
773:         if op == 0x95:
774:             self.pc = p + 1
775:             self._sub(self._dir_read(romb(p)), sfr[SFR_PSW] & 0x80)
776:             return 1
777:         if op in (0x96, 0x97):
778:             self.pc = p
779:             self._sub(ram[self._ri(op & 1)], sfr[SFR_PSW] & 0x80)
780:             return 1
781:         if 0x98 <= op <= 0x9F:
782:             self.pc = p
783:             self._sub(self._r(op & 7), sfr[SFR_PSW] & 0x80)
784:             return 1
785:         # ================================================================ INC
786:         if op in (0x04, 0x05, 0x06, 0x07):
787:             return self._inc_family(op, p, romb)
788:         if 0x08 <= op <= 0x0F:                                     # INC Rn
789:             self.pc = p
790:             n = op & 7
791:             self._set_r(n, (self._r(n) + 1) & 0xFF)
792:             return 1
793:         if op == 0x14:                                             # DEC A
794:             self.pc = p
795:             self.acc = (self.sfr[SFR_ACC] - 1) & 0xFF
796:             return 1
797:         if op in (0x15, 0x16, 0x17):
798:             return self._dec_family(op, p, romb)
799:         if 0x18 <= op <= 0x1F:                                     # DEC Rn
800:             self.pc = p
801:             n = op & 7
802:             self._set_r(n, (self._r(n) - 1) & 0xFF)
803:             return 1
804:         # ================================================================ MUL/DIV
805:         if op == 0xA4:                                             # MUL AB
806:             self.pc = p
807:             result = self.sfr[SFR_ACC] * self.sfr[SFR_B]
808:             self.sfr[SFR_ACC] = result & 0xFF
809:             self.sfr[SFR_B] = (result >> 8) & 0xFF
810:             psw = self.sfr[SFR_PSW] & 0xFE
811:             if result > 0xFF:
812:                 psw |= 0x04
813:             self.sfr[SFR_PSW] = psw
814:             self.set_p()
815:             return 4
816:         if op == 0x84:                                             # DIV AB
817:             self.pc = p
818:             a = self.sfr[SFR_ACC]
819:             b = self.sfr[SFR_B]
820:             psw = self.sfr[SFR_PSW] & 0xFE
821:             if b == 0:
822:                 psw |= 0x04
823:             else:
824:                 self.sfr[SFR_ACC] = a // b
825:                 self.sfr[SFR_B] = a % b
826:             self.sfr[SFR_PSW] = psw
827:             self.set_p()
828:             return 4
829:         # ========================================================== logical ops
830:         if op == 0x54:                                             # ANL A,#imm
831:             self.pc = p + 1
832:             self.acc = self.sfr[SFR_ACC] & romb(p)
833:             return 1
834:         if op == 0x55:
835:             self.pc = p + 1
836:             self.acc = self.sfr[SFR_ACC] & self._dir_read(romb(p))
837:             return 1
838:         if op in (0x56, 0x57):
839:             self.pc = p
840:             self.acc = self.sfr[SFR_ACC] & ram[self._ri(op & 1)]
841:             return 1
842:         if 0x58 <= op <= 0x5F:
843:             self.pc = p
844:             self.acc = self.sfr[SFR_ACC] & self._r(op & 7)
845:             return 1
846:         if op == 0x44:                                             # ORL A,#imm
847:             self.pc = p + 1
848:             self.acc = self.sfr[SFR_ACC] | romb(p)
849:             return 1
850:         if op == 0x45:
851:             self.pc = p + 1
852:             self.acc = self.sfr[SFR_ACC] | self._dir_read(romb(p))
853:             return 1
854:         if op in (0x46, 0x47):
855:             self.pc = p
856:             self.acc = self.sfr[SFR_ACC] | ram[self._ri(op & 1)]
857:             return 1
858:         if 0x48 <= op <= 0x4F:
859:             self.pc = p
860:             self.acc = self.sfr[SFR_ACC] | self._r(op & 7)
861:             return 1

class TestAluFlags(unittest.TestCase):
    """ADD/ADDC/SUBB ОБНОВЛЯЮТ CY/AC/OV, а не только выставляют их.

    «Залипающие» флаги ломают DA A, то есть всю десятичную арифметику денег.
    """

    def _after(self, program: bytes, steps: int = 4) -> CPU8051:
        cpu, _ = make(bytes(program) + b"\x80\xfe")
        cpu.run_steps(steps)
        return cpu

    def test_auxiliary_carry_sets_and_clears(self):
        cpu = self._after([0x74, 0x08, 0x24, 0x08])          # 08h + 08h
        self.assertTrue(cpu.psw & 0x40, "перенос из младшей тетрады -> AC=1")
        cpu = self._after([0x74, 0x10, 0x24, 0x01])          # 10h + 01h
        self.assertFalse(cpu.psw & 0x40, "переноса нет -> AC обязан сброситься")

    def test_carry_sets_and_clears(self):
        cpu = self._after([0x74, 0xFF, 0x24, 0x02])
        self.assertTrue(cpu.psw & 0x80, "FFh+2 -> CY=1")
        cpu = self._after([0x74, 0x01, 0x24, 0x01])
        self.assertFalse(cpu.psw & 0x80, "01h+1 -> CY обязан сброситься")

    def test_overflow_sets_and_clears(self):
        cpu = self._after([0x74, 0x7F, 0x24, 0x01])
        self.assertTrue(cpu.psw & 0x04, "7Fh+1 -> OV=1")
        cpu = self._after([0x74, 0x01, 0x24, 0x01])
        self.assertFalse(cpu.psw & 0x04, "01h+1 -> OV обязан сброситься")

    def test_da_a_gives_correct_bcd(self):
        cpu = self._after([0x74, 0x50, 0x24, 0x00, 0xD4], 5)
        self.assertEqual(cpu.acc, 0x50, "50h+0 -> DA A должно дать 50h")
        cpu = self._after([0x74, 0x09, 0x24, 0x01, 0xD4], 5)
        self.assertEqual(cpu.acc, 0x10, "09h+1 -> DA A должно дать 10h")
        cpu = self._after([0x74, 0x99, 0x24, 0x01, 0xD4], 5)
        self.assertEqual(cpu.acc, 0x00, "99h+1 -> DA A должно дать 00h с переносом")
        self.assertTrue(cpu.psw & 0x80, "CY=1")

    def test_add_preserves_register_bank_bits(self):
        # MOV PSW,#08h (банк 1) ; MOV A,#01h ; ADD A,#01h
        cpu = self._after([0x75, 0xD0, 0x08, 0x74, 0x01, 0x24, 0x01], 6)

demo-fw: FOURTH core bug in m8051/cpu.py — `_da()` checks the high nibble of the PRE-adjustment accumulator, so DA A is wrong whenever the low-nibble +6 carries into the high nibble (0x9A..0x9F). Your flag fix landed (my receipt now prints the correct "12.50 / 15.50"), so this is the last arithmetic blocker: it still corrupts BCD carries, i.e. exactly the money arithmetic.

WHERE (cpu.py `_da`):
    a = self.sfr[SFR_ACC]
    if (a & 0x0F) > 9 or (psw & 0x40):
        a += 6
    if ((self.sfr[SFR_ACC] >> 4) > 9) or carry or (a > 0xFF):   # <-- old A, not `a`
        a += 0x60
        carry = 0x80
Intel's DA A adjusts the low nibble first, then tests the *adjusted* high nibble. As written, 0x9A gets +6 -> 0xA0, but the high-nibble test still looks at 0x9A (high nibble 9) and skips the +0x60, so it returns 0xA0 instead of 0x00 with CY=1.

MEASURED (unmodified core):
    MOV A,#9Ah / DA A             -> A=A0 CY=0   (silicon: A=00 CY=1)
    MOV A,#45h / ADD A,#55h / DA  -> A=A0 CY=0   (silicon: A=00 CY=1, 45+55=100)
    MOV A,#99h / ADD A,#01h / DA  -> A=A0 CY=0   (silicon: A=00 CY=1)
Note the last two start from a *valid* BCD addition — this is not a synthetic edge case, it is how a 4-byte BCD running total overflows a byte.

FIX (one line, evaluate the adjusted value):
    def _da(self, cycles: int) -> int:
        a = self.sfr[SFR_ACC]
        psw = self.sfr[SFR_PSW]
        carry = psw & 0x80
        if (a & 0x0F) > 9 or (psw & 0x40):
            a += 6
        if (a >> 4) > 9 or carry:          # `a` after the low-nibble adjustment
            a += 0x60
            carry = 0x80
        self.sfr[SFR_ACC] = a & 0xFF
        self.sfr[SFR_PSW] = (psw & 0x7F) | carry
        self.set_p()
        return cycles

I am adding these three cases to `TestCoreContract` (DA 0x9A, BCD 45+55, BCD 99+01, each asserting A and CY).

On my side, while waiting: I found my own BCD_SUB4 was wrong independently of the core (I had mis-remembered the "add 0x9A" idiom — its carry comes out as "no borrow = 1", so it does not chain through SUBB correctly; byte 1 came out 0x05 instead of 0x04). I am replacing it with the 10's-complement method (NEG = 10^8 - src computed with a DA-free BCD increment, then dst + NEG), which also keeps CY meaningful: CY=1 after the final byte means dst >= src. Also fixing DRAW_MONEY: it suppressed leading zeros in the wrong direction, so the kopecks cells stayed blank for a whole-ruble value like 1.00.

demo-fw: FOURTH core bug in m8051/cpu.py — `_da()` checks the high nibble of the PRE-adjustment accumulator, so DA A is wrong whenever the low-nibble +6 carries into the high nibble (0x9A..0x9F). Your flag fix landed (my receipt now prints the correct "12.50 / 15.50"), so this is the last arithmetic blocker: it still corrupts BCD carries, i.e. exactly the money arithmetic.

WHERE (cpu.py `_da`):
    a = self.sfr[SFR_ACC]
    if (a & 0x0F) > 9 or (psw & 0x40):
        a += 6
    if ((self.sfr[SFR_ACC] >> 4) > 9) or carry or (a > 0xFF):   # <-- old A, not `a`
        a += 0x60
        carry = 0x80
Intel's DA A adjusts the low nibble first, then tests the *adjusted* high nibble. As written, 0x9A gets +6 -> 0xA0, but the high-nibble test still looks at 0x9A (high nibble 9) and skips the +0x60, so it returns 0xA0 instead of 0x00 with CY=1.

MEASURED (unmodified core):
    MOV A,#9Ah / DA A             -> A=A0 CY=0   (silicon: A=00 CY=1)
    MOV A,#45h / ADD A,#55h / DA  -> A=A0 CY=0   (silicon: A=00 CY=1, 45+55=100)
    MOV A,#99h / ADD A,#01h / DA  -> A=A0 CY=0   (silicon: A=00 CY=1)
Note the last two start from a *valid* BCD addition — this is not a synthetic edge case, it is how a 4-byte BCD running total overflows a byte.

FIX (one line, evaluate the adjusted value):
    def _da(self, cycles: int) -> int:
        a = self.sfr[SFR_ACC]
        psw = self.sfr[SFR_PSW]
        carry = psw & 0x80
        if (a & 0x0F) > 9 or (psw & 0x40):
            a += 6
        if (a >> 4) > 9 or carry:          # `a` after the low-nibble adjustment
            a += 0x60
            carry = 0x80
        self.sfr[SFR_ACC] = a & 0xFF
        self.sfr[SFR_PSW] = (psw & 0x7F) | carry
        self.set_p()
        return cycles

I am adding these three cases to `TestCoreContract` (DA 0x9A, BCD 45+55, BCD 99+01, each asserting A and CY).

On my side, while waiting: I found my own BCD_SUB4 was wrong independently of the core (I had mis-remembered the "add 0x9A" idiom — its carry comes out as "no borrow = 1", so it does not chain through SUBB correctly; byte 1 came out 0x05 instead of 0x04). I am replacing it with the 10's-complement method (NEG = 10^8 - src computed with a DA-free BCD increment, then dst + NEG), which also keeps CY meaningful: CY=1 after the final byte means dst >= src. Also fixing DRAW_MONEY: it suppressed leading zeros in the wrong direction, so the kopecks cells stayed blank for a whole-ruble value like 1.00.

We need to fix the bug in `_da` where the high nibble check uses the pre-adjusted accumulator instead of the post-adjusted value, and verify the correct DA A logic by adjusting the low nibble first, checking if it exceeds 9, then handling the high nibble.I'm also double-checking an edge case with #9A where the low nibble is 0xA (greater than 9), so it adds 6 to get 0xA0, and then the high nibble check correctly adds 0x60 to produce 0x00 with carry set. Now I'm applying both fixes — the `_da` correction and the timer overflow zeroing — and running the full test suite to verify everything works.

172:     """A 12-clocks-per-machine-cycle MCS-51 core."""

184:         self.bus: HardwareBus = bus if bus is not None else NullBus()
185:         self.ram = bytearray(256)          # internal RAM, banked + upper 128
186:         self.sfr = bytearray(256)          # SFR space (direct 0x80..0xFF)
187:         self.pc = 0
188:         self.cycles = 0                    # machine cycles since reset
189:         self.op_count = 0

209:     # ------------------------------------------------------------- lifecycle
210:     def reset(self) -> None:
211:         self.ram[:] = b"\x00" * 256
212:         self.sfr[:] = b"\x00" * 256
213:         self.sfr[SFR_SP] = 0x07
214:         self.sfr[SFR_P0] = 0xFF
215:         self.sfr[SFR_P1] = 0xFF
216:         self.sfr[SFR_P2] = 0xFF
217:         self.sfr[SFR_P3] = 0xFF
218:         self.sfr[SFR_PCON] = 0x00
219:         self._port_latch[:] = b"\xff\xff\xff\xff"
220:         self.pc = 0
221:         self.cycles = 0
222:         self.op_count = 0
223:         self.halted = False
224:         self.error = None
225:         self.missing_pc = None
226:         self.in_isr = 0
227:         self.irq_level = 0
228:         self.idle = False
229:         self.watchdog = 0
230:         self.wd_enabled = False
231:         self.timers_on = False
232:         self._serial_rx = False
233:         self._pending_tick = 0
234: 
235:     # ----------------------------------------------------------------- helpers
236:     @property
237:     def acc(self) -> int:
238:         return self.sfr[SFR_ACC]
239: 
240:     @acc.setter
241:     def acc(self, value: int) -> None:
242:         self.sfr[SFR_ACC] = value & 0xFF
243: 
244:     @property
245:     def psw(self) -> int:
246:         return self.sfr[SFR_PSW]
247: 
248:     @psw.setter
249:     def psw(self, value: int) -> None:
250:         self.sfr[SFR_PSW] = value & 0xFF
251: 
252:     def set_p(self) -> None:
253:         p = _PARITY[self.sfr[SFR_ACC]]
254:         self.sfr[SFR_PSW] = (self.sfr[SFR_PSW] & 0xFE) | p
255: 
256:     @property
257:     def sp(self) -> int:
258:         return self.sfr[SFR_SP]
259: 
260:     @sp.setter
261:     def sp(self, value: int) -> None:
262:         self.sfr[SFR_SP] = value & 0xFF
263: 
264:     @property
265:     def dptr(self) -> int:
266:         return self.sfr[SFR_DPH] << 8 | self.sfr[SFR_DPL]
267: 
268:     @dptr.setter
269:     def dptr(self, value: int) -> None:
270:         self.sfr[SFR_DPH] = (value >> 8) & 0xFF
271:         self.sfr[SFR_DPL] = value & 0xFF
272: 
273:     # register bank helpers (indirect through PSW.RS0/RS1)
274:     def _r(self, n: int) -> int:
275:         return self.ram[((self.sfr[SFR_PSW] >> 3) & 3) * 8 + n]
276: 
277:     def _set_r(self, n: int, v: int) -> None:
278:         self.ram[((self.sfr[SFR_PSW] >> 3) & 3) * 8 + n] = v & 0xFF
279: 
280:     def _ri(self, n: int) -> int:
281:         """Address held in R0/R1 of the active bank."""
282:         return self.ram[((self.sfr[SFR_PSW] >> 3) & 3) * 8 + n]
283: 
284:     # ------------------------------------------------------------------- stack
285:     def push(self, value: int) -> None:
286:         sp = (self.sfr[SFR_SP] + 1) & 0xFF
287:         self.sfr[SFR_SP] = sp
288:         self.ram[sp] = value & 0xFF
289:         if sp <= 7:
290:             self.error = f"stack overflow (SP wrapped to 0x{sp:02X}) at PC=0x{self.pc:04X}"
291: 
292:     def pop(self) -> int:
293:         sp = self.sfr[SFR_SP]
294:         value = self.ram[sp]
295:         self.sfr[SFR_SP] = (sp - 1) & 0xFF
296:         return value
297: 
298:     def push_pc(self) -> None:
299:         """Push the return address the way silicon does: low byte, then high.
300: 
301:         ``RET``/``RETI`` pop the high byte first (see :meth:`pop_pc`), so pushing
302:         high first would byte-swap every return address and corrupt control flow
303:         for every ``LCALL``/``ACALL`` and every interrupt.
304:         """
305:         pc = self.pc
306:         self.push(pc & 0xFF)
307:         self.push(pc >> 8)
308:         if self.in_isr < 8:
309:             self.in_isr += 1
310: 
311:     def pop_pc(self) -> None:
312:         high = self.pop()
313:         low = self.pop()
314:         self.pc = (high << 8) | low
315:         if self.in_isr:
316:             self.in_isr -= 1
317: 
318:     # ------------------------------------------------------------- direct/bit
319:     def _dir_read(self, addr: int) -> int:
320:         if addr < 0x80:
321:             return self.ram[addr]
322:         return self.sfr[addr]
323: 
324:     def _dir_write(self, addr: int, value: int) -> None:
325:         value &= 0xFF
326:         if addr < 0x80:
327:             self.ram[addr] = value
328:             return
329:         if addr == SFR_ACC:
330:             self.sfr[SFR_ACC] = value
331:             self.set_p()
332:             return
333:         if addr == SFR_PSW:
334:             self.sfr[SFR_PSW] = value
335:             return
336:         if SFR_P0 <= addr <= SFR_P3 and (addr & 0x0F) == 0:
337:             # ports need pin/latch interaction
338:             port = (addr - SFR_P0) >> 4
339:             self._port_latch[port] = value
340:             self.sfr[addr] = value
341:             self.bus.port_write(port, value)
342:             return
343:         self.sfr[addr] = value
344:         if addr == SFR_SBUF:
345:             self.bus.serial_write(value)
346:             self.sfr[SFR_SCON] |= SCON_TI
347:         self._sfr_side_effect(addr, value)
348: 
349:     def _port_read(self, port: int) -> int:
350:         """Read a port: latch AND external pin levels (quasi-bidirectional)."""
351:         return self._port_latch[port] & self.bus.port_read(port)
352: 
353:     def _sfr_side_effect(self, addr: int, value: int) -> None:
354:         if addr == SFR_WDTRST:
355:             self.watchdog = 0
356:         elif addr == SFR_WDTPRG:
357:             self.wd_enabled = True
358:         elif addr == SFR_TCON:
359:             self.timers_on = (value & 0x50) != 0
360:         elif addr == SFR_SCON:
361:             self._serial_rx = bool(value & SCON_REN) and self.bus.serial_available()
362: 
363:     # -------------------------------------------------------------------- time
364:     def _advance(self, cycles: int) -> None:
365:         """Run timers/serial/peripherals for ``cycles`` machine cycles."""
366:         self.cycles += cycles
367:         self.op_count += 1
368:         if self.timers_on or self.wd_enabled or self._serial_rx:
369:             self._do_peripherals(cycles)
370:         elif self._pending_tick:
371:             self._pending_tick += cycles
372:             if self._pending_tick >= 32:
373:                 self.bus.tick(self._pending_tick)
374:                 self._pending_tick = 0
375:         else:
376:             self._pending_tick = cycles
377: 
378:     @staticmethod
379:     def _tick_timer(mode: int, th: int, tl: int, cycles: int):
380:         """Advance one 8051 timer by ``cycles`` machine cycles.
381: 
382:         Returns ``(th, tl, overflowed)``.
383: 
384:         On overflow the counter is **zeroed** and the overflow flag is set; any
385:         cycles already consumed by the overflow are discarded, exactly as on
386:         silicon (the flag is set once and the counter restarts from zero - the
387:         interrupt handler has to run before the next overflow matters).
388: 
389:         Each mode has its own arithmetic:
390: 
391:         * mode 0 - 13-bit timer (``TH`` holds 5 bits)
392:         * mode 1 - 16-bit timer
393:         * mode 2 - 8-bit auto-reload: ``TL`` counts, reloads from ``TH``
394:         * mode 3 - split: ``TL`` is an independent 8-bit timer, ``TH`` is
395:           stopped (it belongs to the other timer)
396: 
397:         Note that doing mode 1/0 as one big addition and keeping the remainder
398:         is wrong: 0xFFFE plus 2 cycles must give 0x0000, not 0x0000-plus-zeros
399:         carried over from a 32-bit sum.
400:         """
401:         if mode == 0:
402:             value = ((th & 0x1F) << 8 | tl) + cycles
403:             if value > 0x1FFF:
404:                 return 0x00, 0x00, True
405:             return (value >> 8) & 0x1F, value & 0xFF, False
406:         if mode == 1:
407:             value = (th << 8 | tl) + cycles
408:             if value > 0xFFFF:
409:                 return 0x00, 0x00, True
410:             return (value >> 8) & 0xFF, value & 0xFF, False
411:         if mode == 2:
412:             # TL counts up from its current value to 0xFF, overflows, reloads
413:             # from TH, then counts again.  One overflow takes ``256 - reload``
414:             # cycles, so the batch must be consumed overflow by overflow instead
415:             # of being added to the reloaded value in one go (doing the latter
416:             # corrupts TH, which is the reload register and must never change).
417:             reload = th & 0xFF
418:             period = 256 - reload
419:             remaining = tl + cycles
420:             overflowed = remaining > 0xFF
421:             if overflowed:
422:                 remaining -= 0x100
423:                 while remaining >= period:
424:                     remaining -= period
425:                 value = reload + remaining
426:             else:
427:                 value = remaining
428:             return reload, value & 0xFF, overflowed
429:         # mode 3: only the low half counts, the high half is stopped
430:         value = tl + cycles
431:         if value > 0xFF:
432:             return th & 0xFF, 0x00, True
433:         return th & 0xFF, value & 0xFF, False
434: 
435:     def _do_peripherals(self, cycles: int) -> None:
436:         bus = self.bus
437:         if self._pending_tick:
438:             bus.tick(self._pending_tick + cycles)
439:             self._pending_tick = 0
440:         else:
441:             bus.tick(cycles)
442:         sfr = self.sfr
443:         tmod = sfr[SFR_TMOD]
444:         tcon = sfr[SFR_TCON]
445:         if tcon & TCON_TR0:
446:             th, tl, overflowed = self._tick_timer(
447:                 tmod & 0x03, sfr[SFR_TH0], sfr[SFR_TL0], cycles)
448:             sfr[SFR_TH0] = th
449:             sfr[SFR_TL0] = tl
450:             if overflowed:
451:                 tcon |= TCON_TF0
452:         if tcon & TCON_TR1:
453:             th, tl, overflowed = self._tick_timer(
454:                 (tmod >> 4) & 0x03, sfr[SFR_TH1], sfr[SFR_TL1], cycles)
455:             sfr[SFR_TH1] = th
456:             sfr[SFR_TL1] = tl
457:             if overflowed:
458:                 tcon |= TCON_TF1
459:         sfr[SFR_TCON] = tcon
460:         self.timers_on = (tcon & 0x50) != 0
461:         # serial receive
462:         if self._serial_rx:
463:             chunk = bus.serial_read()
464:             if chunk is not None:
465:                 sfr[SFR_SBUF] = chunk & 0xFF
466:                 sfr[SFR_SCON] |= SCON_RI
467:         # watchdog: 8051 WDT overflows ~ 2**17 machine cycles on AT89C55
468:         if self.wd_enabled:
469:             self.watchdog += cycles
470:             if self.watchdog > 0x20000:
471:                 self.watchdog = 0
472: 
473:     # ------------------------------------------------------------ interrupts
474:     def _poll_interrupts(self) -> None:
475:         ie = self.sfr[SFR_IE]
476:         if not (ie & 0x80):            # EA
477:             return
478:         pending = 0
479:         tcon = self.sfr[SFR_TCON]
480:         if tcon & TCON_IE0:
481:             pending |= IRQ_INT0
482:         if tcon & TCON_TF0:
483:             pending |= IRQ_T0
484:         if tcon & TCON_IE1:
485:             pending |= IRQ_INT1
486:         if tcon & TCON_TF1:
487:             pending |= IRQ_T1
488:         if self.sfr[SFR_SCON] & SCON_RI:
489:             pending |= IRQ_RX
490:         if self.sfr[SFR_SCON] & SCON_TI:
491:             pending |= IRQ_TX
492:         pending |= self.bus.irq_requested()
493:         pending &= 0xFF
494:         if not pending:
495:             return
496:         ip = self.sfr[SFR_IP]
497:         chosen = -1
498:         chosen_pri = -1
499:         for bit, irq in zip(range(6), _VEC_IRQ):
500:             if not (pending & irq):
501:                 continue
502:             if not (ie & irq):
503:                 continue
504:             if (ip & irq) and self.irq_level and irq != self.irq_level:
505:                 continue
506:             pri = 1 if (ip & irq) else 0
507:             if pri > chosen_pri:
508:                 chosen_pri = pri
509:                 chosen = bit
510:         if chosen < 0:
511:             return
512:         irq = _VEC_IRQ[chosen]
513:         if irq == IRQ_T0:
514:             self.sfr[SFR_TCON] &= ~TCON_TF0 & 0xFF
515:         elif irq == IRQ_T1:
516:             self.sfr[SFR_TCON] &= ~TCON_TF1 & 0xFF
517:         elif irq == IRQ_INT0:
518:             self.sfr[SFR_TCON] &= ~TCON_IE0 & 0xFF
519:         elif irq == IRQ_INT1:
520:             self.sfr[SFR_TCON] &= ~TCON_IE1 & 0xFF
521:         elif irq == IRQ_RX:
522:             self.sfr[SFR_SCON] &= ~SCON_RI & 0xFF
523:         elif irq == IRQ_TX:
524:             self.sfr[SFR_SCON] &= ~SCON_TI & 0xFF
525:         self.irq_level = irq if (ip & irq) else 0
526:         self._advance(2)
527:         self.push_pc()
528:         self.pc = _VEC[chosen]
529: 
530:     # ------------------------------------------------------------------- step
531:     def step(self) -> int:
532:         """Execute one instruction.  Returns the machine cycles consumed."""
533:         if self.halted:
534:             return 1
535:         if not self.rom.is_mapped(self.pc):
536:             # Fetching from an address that no code image covers.  On real
537:             # silicon this reads 0xFF (erased EPROM) and the CPU wanders; for
538:             # emulation that is useless, so we stop and report it.
539:             self.missing_pc = self.pc
540:             self.halted = True
541:             self.error = (f"fetch from unmapped code address 0x{self.pc:04X} "
542:                           f"- this part of the firmware image is missing")
543:             return 1
544:         if self.idle:
545:             self._advance(1)
546:             return 1
547:         self._poll_interrupts()
548:         cycles = self._execute()
549:         self._advance(cycles)
550:         return cycles
551: 
552:     def run_steps(self, max_steps: int) -> int:
553:         """Execute at most ``max_steps`` instructions; stop on halt/error."""
554:         executed = 0
555:         while executed < max_steps and not self.halted:
556:             if not self.rom.is_mapped(self.pc):
557:                 self.missing_pc = self.pc
558:                 self.halted = True
559:                 self.error = (f"fetch from unmapped code address 0x{self.pc:04X} "
560:                               f"- this part of the firmware image is missing")
561:                 break
562:             if self.idle:
563:                 self._advance(1)
564:             else:
565:                 self._poll_interrupts()
566:                 self._advance(self._execute())
567:             executed += 1
568:         return executed
569: 
570:     def run(self, cycles: int) -> int:
571:         """Run for at most ``cycles`` machine cycles (or forever if <= 0)."""
572:         executed = 0
573:         target = self.cycles + cycles if cycles > 0 else -1
574:         execute = self._execute
575:         advance = self._advance
576:         mapped = self.rom.is_mapped
577:         while True:
578:             if self.halted:
579:                 break
580:             if self.idle:
581:                 advance(1)
582:             else:
583:                 self._poll_interrupts()
584:                 advance(execute())
585:             executed += 1
586:             if target >= 0 and self.cycles >= target:
587:                 break
588:             if executed >= 400_000_000:
589:                 break
590:             if not mapped(self.pc):
591:                 self.missing_pc = self.pc
592:                 self.halted = True
593:                 self.error = (f"fetch from unmapped code address 0x{self.pc:04X} "
594:                               f"- this part of the firmware image is missing")
595:                 break
596:         return executed
597: 
598:     # --------------------------------------------------------------- execution
599:     def _execute(self) -> int:
600:         rom = self.rom
601:         pc = self.pc
602:         self.last_op = rom.byte(pc)
603:         trace = self.trace
604:         if trace is not None:
605:             if len(trace) < self.trace_limit:
606:                 trace.append((pc, self.last_op, self.acc, self.psw,
607:                               self.sfr[SFR_SP], self.cycles))
608:             else:
609:                 self.trace = None
610:         p = pc + 1
611:         op = self.last_op
612:         romb = rom.byte
613:         sfr = self.sfr
614:         ram = self.ram
615:         bus = self.bus
616:         # ---- decode/execute -------------------------------------------------
617:         if op == 0x00:                                              # NOP
618:             self.pc = p
619:             return 1
620:         # ================================ MOV A, #imm / direct / @Ri / Rn / R
621:         if op == 0x74:                                              # MOV A,#imm
622:             self.pc = p + 1
623:             self.acc = romb(p)
624:             return 1
625:         if op == 0xE5:                                              # MOV A,direct
626:             self.pc = p + 1
627:             addr = romb(p)
628:             if addr == SFR_ACC:
629:                 pass
630:             elif addr < 0x80:
631:                 self.acc = ram[addr]
632:             elif SFR_P0 <= addr <= SFR_P3 and (addr & 0x0F) == 0:
633:                 self.acc = self._port_read((addr - SFR_P0) >> 4)
634:             elif addr == SFR_SBUF:
635:                 self.acc = self.sfr[addr]
636:             else:
637:                 self.acc = self.sfr[addr]
638:             self.set_p()
639:             return 1
640:         if op == 0xF5:                                              # MOV direct,A
641:             self.pc = p + 1
642:             self._dir_write(romb(p), self.sfr[SFR_ACC])
643:             return 1
644:         if op == 0xE4:                                              # CLR A
645:             self.pc = p
646:             self.acc = 0
647:             return 1
648:         if op == 0xF4:                                              # CPL A
649:             self.pc = p
650:             self.acc = self.sfr[SFR_ACC] ^ 0xFF
651:             return 1
652:         if op in (0xE6, 0xE7):                                      # MOV A,@Ri
653:             self.pc = p
654:             self.acc = ram[self._ri(op & 1)]
655:             self.set_p()
656:             return 1
657:         if op in (0xF6, 0xF7):                                      # MOV @Ri,A
658:             self.pc = p
659:             ram[self._ri(op & 1)] = self.sfr[SFR_ACC]
660:             return 1
661:         if op in (0x76, 0x77):                                      # MOV @Ri,#imm
662:             self.pc = p + 1
663:             ram[self._ri(op & 1)] = romb(p)
664:             return 1
665:         if 0xE8 <= op <= 0xEF:                                      # MOV A,Rn
666:             self.pc = p
667:             self.acc = self._r(op & 7)
668:             self.set_p()
669:             return 1
670:         if 0xF8 <= op <= 0xFF:                                      # MOV Rn,A
671:             self.pc = p
672:             self._set_r(op & 7, self.sfr[SFR_ACC])
673:             return 1
674:         if 0x78 <= op <= 0x7F:                                      # MOV Rn,#imm
675:             self.pc = p + 1
676:             self._set_r(op & 7, romb(p))
677:             return 1
678:         if 0xA8 <= op <= 0xAF:                                      # MOV Rn,direct
679:             self.pc = p + 1
680:             self._set_r(op & 7, self._dir_read(romb(p)))
681:             return 1
682:         if 0x88 <= op <= 0x8F:                                      # MOV direct,Rn
683:             self.pc = p + 1
684:             self._dir_write(romb(p), self._r(op & 7))
685:             return 1
686:         if op == 0x85:                                             # MOV direct,direct
687:             self.pc = p + 2
688:             src = romb(p)
689:             dst = romb(p + 1)
690:             self._dir_write(dst, self._dir_read(src))
691:             return 2
692:         if op == 0x75:                                             # MOV direct,#imm
693:             self.pc = p + 2
694:             self._dir_write(romb(p), romb(p + 1))
695:             return 2
696:         if op in (0x86, 0x87):                                     # MOV direct,@Ri
697:             self.pc = p + 1
698:             self._dir_write(romb(p), ram[self._ri(op & 1)])
699:             return 2
700:         if op in (0xA6, 0xA7):                                     # MOV @Ri,direct
701:             self.pc = p + 1
702:             ram[self._ri(op & 1)] = self._dir_read(romb(p))
703:             return 2
704:         if op == 0x90:                                             # MOV DPTR,#imm16
705:             self.pc = p + 2
706:             self.sfr[SFR_DPH] = romb(p)
707:             self.sfr[SFR_DPL] = romb(p + 1)
708:             return 2
709:         # ============================== MOVC / MOVX
710:         if op == 0x93:                                             # MOVC A,@A+DPTR
711:             self.pc = p
712:             self.acc = romb((self.sfr[SFR_ACC] + self.dptr) & 0xFFFF)
713:             return 2
714:         if op == 0x83:                                             # MOVC A,@A+PC
715:             self.pc = p
716:             self.acc = romb((self.sfr[SFR_ACC] + p) & 0xFFFF)
717:             return 2
718:         if op in (0xE2, 0xE3):                                     # MOVX A,@Ri
719:             self.pc = p
720:             addr = self._ri(op & 1)

722:                 addr |= self.sfr[SFR_P2] << 8
723:             self.acc = bus.ext_read(addr) & 0xFF

725:             return 2
726:         if op in (0xF2, 0xF3):                                     # MOVX @Ri,A
727:             self.pc = p
728:             addr = self._ri(op & 1)
729:             self._ext_write_banked(addr, self.sfr[SFR_ACC])
730:             return 2
731:         if op == 0xE0:                                             # MOVX A,@DPTR
732:             self.pc = p
733:             self.acc = bus.ext_read(self.dptr) & 0xFF
734:             self.set_p()
735:             return 2
736:         if op == 0xF0:                                             # MOVX @DPTR,A
737:             self.pc = p
738:             bus.ext_write(self.dptr, self.sfr[SFR_ACC])
739:             return 2
740:         if op == 0xA3:                                             # INC DPTR
741:             self.pc = p
742:             self.dptr = (self.dptr + 1) & 0xFFFF
743:             return 2
744:         # =============================================================== ADD
745:         if op == 0x24:                                             # ADD A,#imm
746:             self.pc = p + 1
747:             self._add(romb(p), 0)
748:             return 1
749:         if op == 0x25:                                             # ADD A,direct
750:             self.pc = p + 1
751:             self._add(self._dir_read(romb(p)), 0)
752:             return 1
753:         if op in (0x26, 0x27):                                     # ADD A,@Ri
754:             self.pc = p
755:             self._add(ram[self._ri(op & 1)], 0)
756:             return 1
757:         if 0x28 <= op <= 0x2F:                                     # ADD A,Rn
758:             self.pc = p
759:             self._add(self._r(op & 7), 0)
760:             return 1
761:         if op == 0x34:                                             # ADDC A,#imm
762:             self.pc = p + 1
763:             self._add(romb(p), sfr[SFR_PSW] & 0x80)
764:             return 1
765:         if op == 0x35:                                             # ADDC A,direct
766:             self.pc = p + 1
767:             self._add(self._dir_read(romb(p)), sfr[SFR_PSW] & 0x80)
768:             return 1
769:         if op in (0x36, 0x37):
770:             self.pc = p
771:             self._add(ram[self._ri(op & 1)], sfr[SFR_PSW] & 0x80)
772:             return 1
773:         if 0x38 <= op <= 0x3F:
774:             self.pc = p
775:             self._add(self._r(op & 7), sfr[SFR_PSW] & 0x80)
776:             return 1
777:         # =============================================================== SUBB
778:         if op == 0x94:
779:             self.pc = p + 1
780:             self._sub(romb(p), sfr[SFR_PSW] & 0x80)
781:             return 1
782:         if op == 0x95:
783:             self.pc = p + 1
784:             self._sub(self._dir_read(romb(p)), sfr[SFR_PSW] & 0x80)
785:             return 1
786:         if op in (0x96, 0x97):
787:             self.pc = p
788:             self._sub(ram[self._ri(op & 1)], sfr[SFR_PSW] & 0x80)
789:             return 1
790:         if 0x98 <= op <= 0x9F:
791:             self.pc = p
792:             self._sub(self._r(op & 7), sfr[SFR_PSW] & 0x80)
793:             return 1
794:         # ================================================================ INC
795:         if op in (0x04, 0x05, 0x06, 0x07):
796:             return self._inc_family(op, p, romb)
797:         if 0x08 <= op <= 0x0F:                                     # INC Rn
798:             self.pc = p
799:             n = op & 7
800:             self._set_r(n, (self._r(n) + 1) & 0xFF)
801:             return 1
802:         if op == 0x14:                                             # DEC A
803:             self.pc = p
804:             self.acc = (self.sfr[SFR_ACC] - 1) & 0xFF
805:             return 1
806:         if op in (0x15, 0x16, 0x17):
807:             return self._dec_family(op, p, romb)
808:         if 0x18 <= op <= 0x1F:                                     # DEC Rn
809:             self.pc = p
810:             n = op & 7
811:             self._set_r(n, (self._r(n) - 1) & 0xFF)
812:             return 1
813:         # ================================================================ MUL/DIV
814:         if op == 0xA4:                                             # MUL AB
815:             self.pc = p
816:             result = self.sfr[SFR_ACC] * self.sfr[SFR_B]
817:             self.sfr[SFR_ACC] = result & 0xFF
818:             self.sfr[SFR_B] = (result >> 8) & 0xFF
819:             psw = self.sfr[SFR_PSW] & 0xFE
820:             if result > 0xFF:
821:                 psw |= 0x04
822:             self.sfr[SFR_PSW] = psw
823:             self.set_p()
824:             return 4
825:         if op == 0x84:                                             # DIV AB
826:             self.pc = p
827:             a = self.sfr[SFR_ACC]
828:             b = self.sfr[SFR_B]
829:             psw = self.sfr[SFR_PSW] & 0xFE
830:             if b == 0:
831:                 psw |= 0x04
832:             else:
833:                 self.sfr[SFR_ACC] = a // b
834:                 self.sfr[SFR_B] = a % b
835:             self.sfr[SFR_PSW] = psw
836:             self.set_p()
837:             return 4
838:         # ========================================================== logical ops
839:         if op == 0x54:                                             # ANL A,#imm
840:             self.pc = p + 1
841:             self.acc = self.sfr[SFR_ACC] & romb(p)
842:             return 1
843:         if op == 0x55:
844:             self.pc = p + 1
845:             self.acc = self.sfr[SFR_ACC] & self._dir_read(romb(p))
846:             return 1
847:         if op in (0x56, 0x57):
848:             self.pc = p
849:             self.acc = self.sfr[SFR_ACC] & ram[self._ri(op & 1)]
850:             return 1
851:         if 0x58 <= op <= 0x5F:
852:             self.pc = p
853:             self.acc = self.sfr[SFR_ACC] & self._r(op & 7)
854:             return 1
855:         if op == 0x44:                                             # ORL A,#imm
856:             self.pc = p + 1
857:             self.acc = self.sfr[SFR_ACC] | romb(p)
858:             return 1
859:         if op == 0x45:
860:             self.pc = p + 1
861:             self.acc = self.sfr[SFR_ACC] | self._dir_read(romb(p))
862:             return 1
863:         if op in (0x46, 0x47):
864:             self.pc = p
865:             self.acc = self.sfr[SFR_ACC] | ram[self._ri(op & 1)]
866:             return 1
867:         if 0x48 <= op <= 0x4F:
868:             self.pc = p
869:             self.acc = self.sfr[SFR_ACC] | self._r(op & 7)
870:             return 1
871:         if op == 0x64:                                             # XRL A,#imm
872:             self.pc = p + 1
873:             self.acc = self.sfr[SFR_ACC] ^ romb(p)
874:             return 1
875:         if op == 0x65:
876:             self.pc = p + 1
877:             self.acc = self.sfr[SFR_ACC] ^ self._dir_read(romb(p))
878:             return 1
879:         if op in (0x66, 0x67):
880:             self.pc = p
881:             self.acc = self.sfr[SFR_ACC] ^ ram[self._ri(op & 1)]
882:             return 1
883:         if 0x68 <= op <= 0x6F:
884:             self.pc = p
885:             self.acc = self.sfr[SFR_ACC] ^ self._r(op & 7)
886:             return 1
887:         # ANL/ORL/XRL direct,A and direct,#imm
888:         if op in (0x52, 0x53):
889:             self.pc = p + (1 if op == 0x52 else 2)
890:             addr = romb(p)
891:             operand = self.sfr[SFR_ACC] if op == 0x52 else romb(p + 1)
892:             self._dir_write(addr, self._dir_read(addr) & operand)
893:             return 1 if op == 0x52 else 2
894:         if op in (0x42, 0x43):
895:             self.pc = p + (1 if op == 0x42 else 2)
896:             addr = romb(p)
897:             operand = self.sfr[SFR_ACC] if op == 0x42 else romb(p + 1)
898:             self._dir_write(addr, self._dir_read(addr) | operand)
899:             return 1 if op == 0x42 else 2
900:         if op in (0x62, 0x63):
901:             self.pc = p + (1 if op == 0x62 else 2)
902:             addr = romb(p)
903:             operand = self.sfr[SFR_ACC] if op == 0x62 else romb(p + 1)
904:             self._dir_write(addr, self._dir_read(addr) ^ operand)
905:             return 1 if op == 0x62 else 2
906:         # =========================================================== rotates
907:         if op == 0x03:                                             # RR A
908:             self.pc = p
909:             a = self.sfr[SFR_ACC]
910:             self.acc = (a >> 1) | ((a & 1) << 7)
911:             return 1
912:         if op == 0x13:                                             # RRC A
913:             self.pc = p
914:             a = self.sfr[SFR_ACC]
915:             carry = 0x80 if (self.sfr[SFR_PSW] & 0x80) else 0

917:             if a & 1:
918:                 psw |= 0x80

920:             self.acc = (a >> 1) | carry
921:             return 1
922:         if op == 0x23:                                             # RL A
923:             self.pc = p
924:             a = self.sfr[SFR_ACC]
925:             self.acc = ((a << 1) | (a >> 7)) & 0xFF
926:             return 1
927:         if op == 0x33:                                             # RLC A
928:             self.pc = p
929:             a = self.sfr[SFR_ACC]
930:             carry_in = 1 if (self.sfr[SFR_PSW] & 0x80) else 0
931:             result = (a << 1) | carry_in
932:             psw = self.sfr[SFR_PSW] & 0x7F
933:             if result > 0xFF:
934:                 psw |= 0x80
935:             self.sfr[SFR_PSW] = psw
936:             self.acc = result & 0xFF
937:             return 1
938:         if op == 0xC4:                                             # SWAP A
939:             self.pc = p
940:             a = self.sfr[SFR_ACC]
941:             self.acc = ((a << 4) | (a >> 4)) & 0xFF
942:             return 1
943:         if op in (0xD4,):                                          # DA A
944:             self.pc = p
945:             return self._da(1)

947:         if op == 0xC5:
948:             self.pc = p + 1
949:             addr = romb(p)
950:             tmp = self._dir_read(addr)
951:             self._dir_write(addr, self.sfr[SFR_ACC])
952:             self.acc = tmp
953:             return 1
954:         if op in (0xC6, 0xC7):
955:             self.pc = p
956:             ri = self._ri(op & 1)
957:             tmp = ram[ri]
958:             ram[ri] = self.sfr[SFR_ACC]

960:             self.set_p()

962:         if 0xC8 <= op <= 0xCF:

964:             n = op & 7
965:             tmp = self._r(n)
966:             self._set_r(n, self.sfr[SFR_ACC])
967:             self.acc = tmp
968:             return 1
969:         if op in (0xD6, 0xD7):                                     # XCHD A,@Ri
970:             self.pc = p
971:             ri = self._ri(op & 1)
972:             a = self.sfr[SFR_ACC]

974:             self.acc = (a & 0xF0) | (ram[ri] & 0x0F)

976:         # ================================================================ PUSH/POP
977:         if op == 0xC0:
978:             self.pc = p + 1
979:             self.push(self._dir_read(romb(p)))

981:         if op == 0xD0:

989:         if op == 0x12:                                             # LCALL
990:             target = romb(p) << 8 | romb(p + 1)

992:             self.push_pc()

994:             return 2
995:         if op == 0x22:                                             # RET
996:             self.pop_pc()
997:             return 2
998:         if op == 0x32:                                             # RETI
999:             self.pop_pc()

1002:         if op in (0x01, 0x21, 0x41, 0x61, 0x81, 0xA1, 0xC1, 0xE1):  # AJMP
1003:             page = (p & 0xF800)
1004:             target = page | ((op >> 5) << 8) | romb(p)

1007:         if op in (0x11, 0x31, 0x51, 0x71, 0x91, 0xB1, 0xD1, 0xF1):  # ACALL
1008:             page = (p & 0xF800)

1010:             self.pc = p + 1
1011:             self.push_pc()

1013:             return 2

1015:             self.pc = (p + 1 + _signed(romb(p))) & 0xFFFF

1017:         if op == 0x40:                                             # JC
1018:             self.pc = (p + 1 + _signed(romb(p))) & 0xFFFF if (sfr[SFR_PSW] & 0x80) else p + 1

1020:         if op == 0x50:                                             # JNC
1021:             self.pc = p + 1 if (sfr[SFR_PSW] & 0x80) else (p + 1 + _signed(romb(p))) & 0xFFFF

1023:         if op == 0x60:                                             # JZ
1024:             self.pc = (p + 1 + _signed(romb(p))) & 0xFFFF if self.sfr[SFR_ACC] == 0 else p + 1

1026:         if op == 0x70:                                             # JNZ
1027:             self.pc = p + 1 if self.sfr[SFR_ACC] == 0 else (p + 1 + _signed(romb(p))) & 0xFFFF

1030:             left, right = self.sfr[SFR_ACC], romb(p)

1036:         if op == 0xB5:                                             # CJNE A,direct,rel
1037:             left, right = self.sfr[SFR_ACC], self._dir_read(romb(p))
1038:             self.pc = p + 2
1039:             self._cjne(left, right)
1040:             if left != right:
1041:                 self.pc = (p + 2 + _signed(romb(p + 1))) & 0xFFFF
1042:             return 2
1043:         if op in (0xB6, 0xB7):                                     # CJNE @Ri,#imm,rel
1044:             left, right = ram[self._ri(op & 1)], romb(p)
1045:             self.pc = p + 2
1046:             self._cjne(left, right)

1048:                 self.pc = (p + 2 + _signed(romb(p + 1))) & 0xFFFF
1049:             return 2
1050:         if 0xB8 <= op <= 0xBF:                                     # CJNE Rn,#imm,rel
1051:             left, right = self._r(op & 7), romb(p)

1053:             self._cjne(left, right)

1055:                 self.pc = (p + 2 + _signed(romb(p + 1))) & 0xFFFF
1056:             return 2
1057:         if op == 0xD5:                                             # DJNZ direct,rel
1058:             addr = romb(p)

1063:         if 0xD8 <= op <= 0xDF:                                     # DJNZ Rn,rel
1064:             n = op & 7

1068:             return 2

1070:             bit = self._bit(romb(p))

{"file_path": "C:\Проекты VS\C проги и пай клиенты\test1\test\tests\test_cpu.py", "new_string": "class TestCJNE(unittest.TestCase):
    """CJNE переходит при НЕРАВЕНСТВЕ; CY ставится отдельно (left < right)."""

    def _branch_program(self, cjne: bytes, setup: bytes = b""):
        """Собрать: <setup> ; CJNE <cjne> ; LJMP NO ; LJMP YES.

        ``cjne`` — это опкод и операнды БЕЗ байта смещения; смещение
        подставляется так, чтобы переход вёл на ``LJMP YES``.
        """
        program = bytearray(setup)
        cjne_at = len(program)
        program += bytes(cjne)                       # ровно 2 байта операндов
        program += b"\x02"                           # смещение: на 2 байта вперёд
        no_at = len(program)
        program += bytes([0x02, 0x00, 0x40])         # сюда, если НЕ перешли
        yes_at = len(program)
        program += bytes([0x02, 0x00, 0x80])         # сюда, если перешли
        program += bytes(0x80 - len(program))
        cpu, _ = make(bytes(program))
        return cpu, no_at, yes_at

    def _run_cjne(self, cjne: bytes, setup: bytes = b"", setup_steps: int = 1):
        cpu, no_at, yes_at = self._branch_program(cjne, setup)
        cpu.run_steps(setup_steps)
        cpu.step()                                   # сама CJNE
        return cpu, no_at, yes_at

        # ``CARRY1(a, b)`` is Ghidra's name for "does a + b carry out of bit 7".

        def carry1(a, b, _c=None):
            return 1 if (int(a) & 0xFF) + (int(b) & 0xFF) > 0xFF else 0

        def carry2(a, b, _c=None):
            return 1 if (int(a) & 0xFFFF) + (int(b) & 0xFFFF) > 0xFFFF else 0

tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. A stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) end the whole script instead of producing `null`. The script has no filesystem, network, timer, or Node.js APIs; the agents do the work.

tools.name: pwsh
tools.description: Execute a PowerShell command (`pwsh -Command`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh pwsh process; pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Paths use native Windows form (`C:\...`); read environment variables with `$env:NAME`. Managed `$env:DSH_*` variables expose current harness environment facts. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. On Windows a force-killed command settles as `[exit code: 1]` without a signal marker — treat it as an interruption, not a command failure. Before any delete or move, verify that the resolved absolute target path is the intended one; never run it against a computed path you have not checked. Do not assign to automatic variables such as `$HOME`; variable names are case-insensitive, so `$home` is the same read-only variable. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]`, a policy denial: do not retry another way. Under the Windows sandbox, read-only pwsh runs in PowerShell ConstrainedLanguage mode, while workspace-write stays in FullLanguage unless host policy says otherwise. In read-only, prefer cmdlets and core types (`[string]`, `[datetime]`, `[regex]`, `[guid]`); .NET static calls (`[System.IO.*]::`, `[math]::`), `Add-Type`, COM objects, and reflection fail with "only core types" errors. `-f` formatting, property access, and core cmdlets work. In both confined modes, programs cannot open named pipes, so a command that captures another program's output through piped stdio (Node.js `child_process.spawn`/`exec` with the default `stdio: 'pipe'`) fails with EPERM, while `stdio: 'inherit'` and `stdio: 'ignore'` spawns work and PowerShell's own pipelines are unaffected.
